feature: a Jolt proof of the agent's pick made in the visitor's own browser: the `decide` guest reprices all 8 hotel offers with the contract's price rule (`zkcore`) and checks the pick is listed, priced by code, inside the budget and the cheapest that fits; the page verifies the proof and refuses the same proof for a claim changed by one unit
short: a Jolt proof of the agent's pick made and checked in the visitor's own browser; not zero-knowledge, not checked on chain
where: `agents/prove.html`, `agents/prove/`, `agents/coi-prove-sw.js`, `zk/browser/` (its own Jolt pin `b4eb62480d76`, separate from the four guests the contract anchors)
detail: 39,159 cycles; native prove 1.53 s, verify 28 ms, proof 78,527 bytes; headless Chrome 5.7 to 15 s on 8 threads across runs (the page's own service worker adds the isolation headers a static host cannot send) and 21 s on one thread, byte-identical proof both ways; not zero-knowledge (every input is public), verified in the page and not on chain; no phone timed yet; the two wasm32 fixes are upstream's (a16z/jolt#1913, 0xAndoroid/jolt-wasm-prover)

feature: NEAR AI issues the verdict under E2EE v2: the facts go sealed to the attested model key, the model derives the predicates and echoes a binding of the envelope, and `make verify` checks the TDX quote (dcap-qvl, Intel root, committed PCS collateral), report_data (signing key and our nonce), the TEE signature over the exact wire bytes, the sealed answer (opened with its disclosed per-field key), predicates equal to the code's, and the binding
short: NEAR AI issues the verdict under E2EE v2: facts sealed to the attested model key; `make verify` checks the TDX quote and the TEE signature offline
detail: one testnet purchase with a verdict glm-5.3-flash issued (`make model-buy`, 2026-11-05): the facts sealed to the model key registered against its on-chain TDX quote verification, `submit_near_ai_verdict` accepted it (issuer `near-ai:5a0210f2..`), the eval-gated merchant refused it (v4 bucket 50, under 70), m01 settled 36 dUSDC, the replay refused; `make verify-live` re-checks it. one live capture on synthetic facts (chat `08af1d014f2d4f379dba94094562d9ba`, TCB UpToDate). On chain, `submit_near_ai_verdict` accepts it only with a registered model attestation (same nonce), the TEE signature over the exact response bytes, and a sealed answer that opens with the disclosed key and echoes this envelope's binding; `make verify` runs the contract on it and on 4 refusals. The quote check itself happens before `register_model_attestation`, not in the contract; the NVIDIA GPU evidence is checked offline from NVIDIA's signed NRAS reply (`scripts/nras.mjs`)

feature: OutLayer worker as referee: signed result (<= 900 bytes) checked by the contract with `ed25519_verify`; `settle` requires the receipt
detail: testnet, 2026-11-14: the component runs on OutLayer as `bookerbob.testnet/bookerbob-referee` (active version `6fca1eaa`, rebuilt from public `1d39cd6` with the release's `build.sh` at any checkout path, on macOS arm64 with rustc 1.96.0), its TEE-derived key is a registered referee; one dUSDC purchase settled under the receipt `request_referee` brought back from OutLayer, one cheat claim refused by it with its settle blocked; `make verify-live` re-derives both. Inputs sealed X25519 only (the post-quantum key exceeds one OutLayer output); each run's TDX quote verified on chain by our DCAP verifier and bound to its wasm, input and output (`scripts/outlayer-attest.mjs`), OutLayer's keystore still trusted; the project's owner (the BookerBob operator) can publish a version that signs with the same key (`docs/outlayer.md`). Mainnet, 2026-11-14: the same wasm as a project owned by the mainnet bazaar, its key a registered referee beside ours, one 0.9025 USDC purchase settled under its receipt (`node scripts/mainnet-outlayer.mjs check`, `docs/keyless.md`)

feature: dispute arbiter: re-checks citations and every signature, signs upheld or overturned; an overturned receipt is cleared and settle is blocked
detail: `make verify` check 22; live on testnet since 2026-11-14 on OutLayer: the project's arbiter host key (registered through the anchor timelock) overturned a receipt our referee key forged for a cheat, the receipt was cleared and settle refused (`node scripts/outlayer-dispute.mjs verify`). Since then the live bazaar runs at threshold 2: every decision needs our arbiter key and the OutLayer key (`set_arbiter_threshold`, `submit_dispute_decisions`, 4 contract tests)

feature: sealed reviews (Semaphore v4): a settled purchase joins the merchant's group (LeanIMT, Poseidon on chain); during a round a member posts a sealed rating with a Groth16 proof checked on `alt_bn128` host functions, one per member per round (nullifier scoped to merchant and round); after the round members reveal, only if the group has k >= 5 and the round holds at least 5 distinct raters (k_d, since 2026-11-12); release is batched and sorted by hash; `best_quote` breaks price ties by the score and takes a `min_score` floor
short: sealed reviews (Semaphore v4): a buyer who paid rates anonymously, a Groth16 proof is checked on chain, ratings open only at 5 members and 5 raters a round
detail: 3 rounds of 6 sealed ratings released on testnet (2 for m01, 1 for h05); 13 contract tests on real Semaphore proofs

feature: conserved delegation: standing flows from a merchant's released ratings along hire edges to the sub-agents it hires (w = 1/2), following a design rule in REP's draft "(an unpublished REP draft)": the whole chain gets at most w/(1-w) of the seed
short: conserved delegation: standing flows from a merchant's ratings along hire edges at 1/2, capped for the whole chain
detail: standing flowed from m01's released ratings to m02 and m03 on testnet; property test over random graphs with rings

feature: verifiable compute (Jolt zkVM), four guests: standing graph, price stack, referee, cohort k >= 5. The contract keeps the graph root and per-cohort roots; for the graph, the contract keeps a hash-chained root of the standing graph and accepts a score update only when it names the registered program hash, is for the current root and is signed by a bonded worker key that verified the proof off chain. The contract verifies no proof, so it cannot itself tell which program produced the scores
short: Jolt zkVM, four guests (standing graph, price, referee, cohort). The contract verifies no proof: a bonded worker key signs that it did
detail: all four guests proved and verified (prove 1.3 to 9 s, verify about 60 ms, proofs 80 to 93 KB); standing proved twice over the live graph and posted on testnet

short: proven standing tree: one root on chain, no scores stored; a merchant proves its rank, so the chain answers "is X in the top N%"

short: post-quantum: the sealed referee input is hybrid (X25519 + ML-KEM-768); the README says per piece what holds and what does not
detail: v1 sealing tests (round trip, swapped KEM ciphertext, downgrade), the contract checks a v1 input's 1,088-byte KEM ciphertext; brute-force tests on the commitment, claims and proof hashes; signatures and Jolt (BN254) are still classical

feature: the NEAR AI model's TDX quote verified on chain: Intel DCAP checks (a dcap-qvl fork) in five calls, and the bazaar registers a model key only against a finalized verification whose report_data is that key and nonce
short: the NEAR AI model's TDX quote verified on chain (Intel DCAP, five calls); the bazaar registers a model key only against that result

feature: REP Eval, calibrated: 120 sealed items at 4 levels, 3 NEAR AI models in a 400-token budget, every answer TEE-signed, grading and a bootstrap 95% CI in the worker's code, one certificate per model from a separate eval issuer key; a leaderboard page reads the scores from chain
short: REP Eval, calibrated: 120 sealed items, 3 NEAR AI models, every answer TEE-signed, a 95% CI, a leaderboard read from chain

Only one model lands in the 40 to 80% band. v2 (protocol frozen first): 60 referee-claim items, truth from the referee's code, set committed by its own owner account with `commit_eval_set`: glm 44/60, DeepSeek 35/60, Qwen a budget probe at 0; every answer given was right, every miss a reply cut at 600 tokens; v3, the same items at 2,000 tokens (frozen first): DeepSeek 58/60, glm 55/60, again right on every answer given, so the set is too easy to separate them by accuracy

feature: REP Eval v4 and the eval gate: 40 harder referee-claim items (truth from the referee's code, protocol frozen before the set), and `set_eval_gate`: a merchant sells only to a verdict issued by a NEAR AI model whose certificate passes `eval_passes`
short: REP Eval v4 and the eval gate: a merchant sells only to a verdict from a model whose certificate passes the threshold
detail: v4 on testnet: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 29/40 (bucket 70), glm-5.3-flash 22/40 (bucket 50, the first wrong finished answer in any run); `vetted` gated on v4 at 70 until 2026-11-06 (now the v5 lower bound), an ordinary verdict's receipt was refused on chain; a glm-issued verdict was refused by the gate and bought from m01 instead (`make model-buy`); DeepSeek, its key registered against its on-chain TDX verification, passed under the v4 point-bucket rule and bought from `vetted` (the v5 lower-bound rule would refuse it) (`MODEL_BUY_MODEL=... make model-buy`); the 70 was set after the v4 scores; `make eval-gate`, `make eval-verify`

feature: REP Eval v5: 120 items, protocol committed first, the gate on the Wilson 95% lower bound (threshold 70 fixed before the set), certified apart as `/ci95-lower` with no contract change, truncation reported apart
short: REP Eval v5: 120 items, protocol committed first, the gate on the Wilson 95% lower bound
detail: both bazaars: DeepSeek 91/120 (lower bound 67.4), glm 88/120 (64.8): both in point bucket 70, neither passes 70 on the bound, and `vetted` gates on the bound, so both are refused live (DeepSeek's verdict refused on chain, `make eval-gate`); `make eval-verify` recomputes the bound and reads `eval_passes`

feature: NEAR Intents: one agent-to-agent settlement on mainnet; 1Click top-up planned
short: NEAR Intents: one agent-to-agent settlement on mainnet; 1Click top-up planned
detail: ran once on mainnet: the buyer agent's own signed NEP-413 transfer intent moved 0.1 wNEAR to the merchant agent inside intents.near (execute_intents 42TLj4c7MKCcLUHP6HqB91LDcMqC6ZRdBzHem8BbmpVz, memo naming testnet purchase 9Esa4qik), re-read keyless by `node scripts/intents-settle.mjs check` and `make mainnet-check`. feature: history anchor: NEAR as the history and backup layer for a market that runs on another chain. A contract stores hash-chained round roots from one pinned poster (next seq, previous head, no rewrite, no delete); `make arc-anchor-rebuild` rebuilds the foreign market's groups, members, nullifiers and lists from its own events and checks every root and the chain against NEAR
short: history anchor: hash-chained round roots of our Arc testnet market on NEAR; `make arc-anchor-rebuild` checks that market against them
detail: live on testnet at `bookerbob-anchor.testnet`: 55 rounds of our Arc testnet market (from our ETHGlobal Mumbai build) posted, rebuild PASS over 1,255 Arc logs, a locally changed log fails at its own round; it proves the posted history cannot change, not that the foreign events are true; the poster and the account key are ours; the bazaar's own rounds do not post to it yet

feature: one price for a batch (`propose_clearing`, design: Dan, DenisDI): after a round's reveal closes anyone submits a seating; the contract opens each budget commitment, prices every seat with its own code, requires quote <= price <= budget and price == the highest quote seated, and keeps the proposal with more seats, or the same seats at a lower price. The search stays outside; the contract checks bounds
short: one price for a batch (`propose_clearing`, design: Dan, DenisDI): the contract method is on the branch `clearing`, not on testnet
where: `docs/clearing.md`, `sdk/clearing.mjs`, `agents/clearing.html`, `fixtures/clearing.json`; the contract method and its tests are on the branch `clearing`
detail: not deployed and not on main's contract: a new money path does not go live before the submission. On the branch: 27 contract tests (Dan's three worked examples; refused: a price above the highest quote, a budget below the price, more seats than declared, a participant twice, before reveal closes, a worse proposal does not replace the standing one, replay) and a byte-for-byte check that the stored state layout is unchanged; the reference solver gives the same answers in Rust and JS

feature: bucketed schedules shrink the price leak (L10): the bits a sale's amount reveals, measured per merchant; one discount on every rule with the cap equal to it, so several bit sets pay one price
short: bucketed schedules: several proven bit sets pay one price, so the amount reveals less (L10)
detail: amount channel only: on the swarm's own sales, given the merchant, 1.00 bit per sale, 0.00 bucketed because every swarm set holds world_id_human, which those buckets price; mean over 30 schedules with every swarm set assumed at every merchant 1.03 to 0.41, none over 1 bit, 14 of the 16 zero-leak schedules resting on that same fact; merchant choice still tells about 1.5 bits in hoodie, untouched by bucketing; the worst-hit bit set pays up to 10.25% of base more against a group price (m01, k >= 5), 8.8% at k = 0; `make leak-amount` fails a bucketed merchant over its design bound; on testnet 5 buyers paid 40.92 dUSDC at `bkt-m01.bookerbob-demo.testnet`, their bit sets as we recorded them (sealed on chain), the equal price by construction (`make bucketed-check`, re-read by `make verify-live`)

feature: coalitions against single agents, pre-registered: members admitted by the bazaar's own `in_top` proof over the proven review-score tree, bonded, a no-show slashed; a sybil ring with fabricated hire edges has no leaf and is refused
short: coalitions with proven standing and bonds against single agents (a pre-registered simulation)
detail: pre-registration sha256 on testnet before the first seed ran (tx [4KZDqTwj…](https://testnet.nearblocks.io/txns/4KZDqTwjUAT7Yq3pX2wXfTzawYGVQ6Mk35kEr1W289z5), `node scripts/prereg-anchor.mjs check`; the code was not anchored, its sha256 is in the result); 20 seeds: admission by the proven review-score tree fills 83.4% of bundles against 64.5% for single agents, failed legs per 100 bundles 17.3 against 40.8, wins 20, 19 and 20 of 20 seeds (rule: 18); the bonds cut net buyer loss by 21% of the gap to single agents with no filter (17 of 20 seeds cheaper all in, counting the 2% carry); exploratory, beyond the pre-registration: single agents applying the same filter with no bond fill 83.7%, so the fill gain is the standing filter, and with unreliable agents at 80% to 90% the fill gain is gone (79.5% each); sybils: 3 forgery types, each refused in all 160 epoch states; 4.9% dearer per filled bundle, 2 of those points the carry; a simulation with our parameters, `make coalition-check` re-runs it; the hire-edge fan-out is proven alongside and does not rank admission yet (standing v2 would)

feature: coalitions of merchant agents: a multi-leg job admits a member only on the bazaar's `in_top` proof of its proven standing, holds it by a dUSDC bond, and on finalize pays the deliverers pro rata and slashes a no-show to the buyer and the deliverers
short: coalitions: members admitted by a proof of standing, bonded; a no-show slashed on chain
where: `coalition/src/lib.rs` (v3, 29 tests; v1 and v2 as they ran in `coalition/v1/`, `coalition/v2/`), `scripts/coalition-live.mjs`, `docs/coalitions.md`
detail: on testnet. Coalition v3 (`coalition-v3.bookerbob-demo.testnet`): only the purchase's own named buyer agent can announce it, while unspent; a leg keeps up to 4 announced purchases and delivers with any of them that settled; a leg with no announced purchase is released; a no-show's bond goes half to the buyer, half to the treasury. In job E the treasury and the lead are both ours (the BookerBob operator), so we received the whole slash; the next deploy makes the Sputnik DAO the treasury and sends it the whole slash. Job E: two announces on one leg, the earlier one delivered, a cross-agent announce refused on chain, h05 slashed (finalize [EXa1pwtg…](https://testnet.nearblocks.io/txns/EXa1pwtgyE2QTcwTR2d9s2xSeHmELcL7WEBhHNpQCC4t)). Jobs A to C ran on v1 (m02 had no opening in the n=2 tree, so it could present no proof and was refused; 5 paid sealed reviews seeded it, the graph was re-proved in Jolt, and it was admitted), D on v2; each version's gaps are in the doc. `make coalition-verify` 43 checks over public RPC, plus 29 contract tests; all accounts ours, dUSDC a test token, the three coalition accounts keep their deploy keys

feature: admission by the hire-edge fan-out (standing v2, v3, and v3 cut by count as v4): each ranking pre-registered on testnet before its run and measured against v1; every one missed its rule, and admission stays on v1
short: admission by the hire-edge fan-out: three pre-registered attempts, each a published FAIL
detail: anchors [7stwAQ6Q…](https://testnet.nearblocks.io/txns/7stwAQ6QJaZdf4aJD8ERngkvN8k3jkSqU3ecTAbijz3J), [kCHZBSZZ…](https://testnet.nearblocks.io/txns/kCHZBSZZ1u89h4HKG9HV7RNjSHQwJ1Rbe7pj9KPfcoQ), [DwZPkVsi…](https://testnet.nearblocks.io/txns/DwZPkVsiV2qkY1n4WpbV6S5oKUy6A2hjfAbvhhHsAQgX); v2: volume buys rank, failed legs 23.7 against 17.3; v3: newcomers in 20 of 20 seeds but the longer list lets unreliable agents past the cut, 21.6 against 17.3; v4 on fresh seeds 21 to 40: as safe as v1 (18.9 against 19.1 failed legs, fill 0.817 against 0.812) with 1.6 reliable newcomers per seed, short of the registered 18 of 20 seeds (16); sybil rings 0 in every attempt; `make coalition-v4-check`

feature: Jolt proofs verified inside OutLayer's TEE: a component pins programs by hash, verifies a proof with Jolt 997c1543's verifier and signs accept or reject; a registry contract admits only a signed accept
detail: testnet, 2026-11-14: project `bookerbob.testnet/bookerbob-jolt-verify` (wasm `cad8d2e1`, fixed-path build); the standing proof behind the bazaar's root (program `c780ceab`) got a signed accept whose output is that root, a forged proof a signed reject; `smith-reg.bookerbob-demo.testnet` took the accept and refused the reject; its TDX quote verified on chain by our DCAP verifier; OutLayer's keystore and the project owner still trusted
short: Jolt proofs verified inside OutLayer's TEE, a signed accept admitted by a registry contract

feature: economy anchor: agent reputation as a public NEAR record. The public events of nine BookerBob testnet contracts (bazaar bids, verdicts, settles, referee and arbiter results, hires and review seeds, standing roots; coalition joins, deliveries, slashes and payouts; dUSDC transfers; smith registry programs) are cut into hourly epochs and posted to an open anchor contract: anyone posts, one chain per poster and source, the contract hashes the records itself and refuses out-of-order, duplicate, wrong-epoch or open-epoch records; `make anchor-check` compares the anchor with the watched contracts' txs and checks the graph and coalition job counters for gaps, `make anchor-rebuild` rebuilds agent outcomes and the proven standing from the anchor's posts alone
short: economy anchor: nine contracts' events chained hourly on NEAR; `make anchor-rebuild` rebuilds outcomes and the standing root from it
detail: live on testnet at `bookerbob-outcomes.testnet` since 2026-11-14: 42 hourly epochs, 3,241 events, head `143a000d`; anchor-check PASS (graph events 1..10 equal the bazaar's graph_root at the last anchored block, coalition job ids complete there), a locally changed event fails at its epoch; anchor-rebuild PASS: 6 of 6 coalition (contract, member) records equal the contracts' member() views, and the standing rebuilt from the anchor's 10 graph events equals the bazaar's on-chain standing_root `3b5db5e9`; completeness is partial (counters cover graph events and coalition jobs only; discovery trusts the indexer); a first chain with rounded timestamps is superseded; the same 42 epochs on NEAR mainnet at the implicit account `a145dcce`, head `796e89ab`, with anchor-check and anchor-rebuild PASS against it (0.035 NEAR burnt, 1.557 NEAR storage); the poster and the account key are ours

feature: the evaluator inside OutLayer's TEE: buyer facts sealed to it, the TLSNotary presentation verified there, the verdict signed by a key only the TEE holds and accepted by the bazaar as an issuer
short: the evaluator in OutLayer's TEE: buyer facts sealed to it and checked there (v0 live; v1 fixes its audited issues in code)
detail: testnet, 2026-11-14: v0 is deployed as project `bookerbob.testnet/bookerbob-evaluator` (release `evaluator-v0`); the founder's signed-in GitHub presentation was sealed to the TEE's X25519 key, verified there with upstream TLSNotary, and a verdict signed by the TEE key was accepted by the bazaar under that key registered as an issuer; a predicate the facts do not back got a signed refusal. The audit of v0 found issues (`docs/outlayer-eval.md`, `docs/audit.md` E1 to E12), and on the locked bazaar v0's issuer key cannot be revoked. v1 fixes them in code with tests (sha256 `4d2c4a3b…`), not deployed: the locked bazaar cannot register it. `make outlayer-eval-verify` re-derives the v0 run keylessly (20 checks)
